title: Monthly High-Dose Vitamin D Treatment for the Prevention of Functional Decline: A Randomized Clinical Trial
authors: Bischoff-Ferrari HA, Dawson-Hughes B, Orav EJ, Staehelin HB, Meyer OW, Theiler R, et al.
population: Community-dwelling men and women aged 70 years or older with a prior fall, Zurich, Switzerland; 58.0% had 25-hydroxyvitamin D below 20 ng/mL at baseline
funder: The primary funding sources for this trial were professorship grant PP00B-114864 from the Swiss National Science Foundation and The VELUX Foundations. Supplementary funding was provided by investigator-initiated funds from Merck Sharp & Dohme AG, WILD, and DSM Nutritional Products. The funding sources had no role in the design and conduct of the study; collection, management, analysis, and interpretation of the data; preparation, review, or approval of the manuscript; and decision to submit the manuscript for publication.
authorConflicts: Bischoff-Ferrari: speaker fees from and advisory boards for Merck Sharp & Dohme AG, Amgen, WILD, DSM Nutritional Products, Roche Diagnostics, Nestlé, Pfizer and Sanofi. No other disclosures were reported.
result: Monthly vitamin D3 24,000 IU (control), 60,000 IU, or 24,000 IU plus calcifediol 300 µg for one year. Lower extremity function did not differ between groups (P=0.26). Incidence of falls: 66.9% (95% CI 54.4% to 77.5%) with 60,000 IU and 66.1% (53.5% to 76.8%) with 24,000 IU plus calcifediol, against 47.9% (35.8% to 60.3%) with 24,000 IU (P=0.048); mean number of falls 1.47, 1.24 and 0.94 (P=0.09).
